# Translation quality review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Vue2 Options API SFC owns the visit; outlet capability captures instance state and real destroy retires listeners.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

<template><section><textarea :value="current ? current.text : ''" @input="edit($event.target.value)"></textarea><button @click="submit">Accept translation</button></section></template>
<script>
import {trailing,bindConfirmation} from './services.js';
export default {
  props: ['services'],
  data() { return {current: null, navigation: 0, env: this.services}; },
  beforeDestroy() { this.close(); },
  methods: { getVisit() { return this.current; }, setVisit(value) { this.current=value; },
retire() {
  const leaving = this.getVisit();
  this.setVisit(null);
  if (leaving) {
    leaving.task.flush();
    leaving.stop();
  }
  if (!this.getVisit()) this.env.renderDocument(null);
},
open(id) {
  this.env.renderSubmission(null);
  const request = ++this.navigation;
  this.retire();
  if (request !== this.navigation) return;

  const stop = this.env.store.subscribe(event => { if (event.id === id) this.env.renderStatus(event); });
  const task = trailing(this.env.timers, 120, text => this.env.store.write(id, text));
  const visit = {id, text: this.env.store.read(id), stop, task};
  this.setVisit(visit); this.env.renderDocument({id, text: visit.text});
},
edit(text) {
  const visit = this.getVisit(); if (!visit) return;
  visit.text = text;
  visit.task.push(text);
},
close() { this.env.renderSubmission(null); ++this.navigation; this.retire(); },
submit() {
  const confirmation=bindConfirmation(()=>this.getVisit(),receipt=>this.env.renderSubmission(receipt));
  const visit = this.getVisit(); if (!visit) return null;
  const snapshot = {id: visit.id, text: visit.text};
  visit.task.flush();
  const receipt = this.env.archive.capture(snapshot);
  confirmation.show(receipt);
  return receipt;
},

  },
};
</script>

checkpoints: Within one editor visit, make several edits less than 120 ms apart: no store write occurs before quiet expiry, and exactly one write containing the latest text occurs after 120 ms of quiet.
After the first burst saves, edit again and verify a new 120 ms quiet interval produces a second write with that burst's latest text.
Open, close, or dispose with a pending edit and verify the latest text is persisted synchronously, the scheduled execution is consumed, and advancing timers produces no duplicate write.
Submit with a pending edit and verify persistence settles before archive capture, while submit still synchronously returns that capture's receipt.
Cause store-write or archive listeners to navigate during submission; the originating snapshot remains captured, stale confirmation is suppressed, and a newer visit is not replaced or cleared.
Verify open still restores persisted text, close still clears the document and submission outputs when no reentrant newer visit exists, and submit returns null with no selected editor.
Verify search preview behavior remains unchanged: it publishes after its existing 40 ms quiet interval and hide cancels unpublished work.
forbidden_effects: Do not continue writing on every keystroke.
Do not lose the latest accepted edit when a visit is opened over, closed, submitted, or disposed before the timer expires.
Do not allow a consumed timer callback to write the same burst again.
Do not let an older visit's flush or completion overwrite, clear, or publish confirmation into a newer visit.
Do not infer visit ownership from document id or receipt contents; reopening the same document creates a distinct visit.
Do not alter the adjacent search preview or its 40 ms behavior.
Do not make open, edit, close, submit, or dispose asynchronous, and do not change the injected store, archive/queue, timer, render, or outlet interfaces.
lifecycle_identity: Each call to open creates a fresh editor-visit identity, even when reopening the same document id.
The trailing edit task belongs to the visit created by open and writes using that visit's captured document id.
A submission snapshot and acquired confirmation outlet belong to the visit active when submit begins.
Archive capture is a durable effect for the originating snapshot; visible confirmation is permitted only while that exact originating visit remains current.
The existing navigation generation must prevent an outer open operation from installing an obsolete visit after callback-capable retirement work starts a newer navigation.

obligations.text: Replace immediate per-keystroke persistence with the visit's existing 120 ms trailing task: every edit updates visit.text immediately and pushes that text to the task.
For each uninterrupted editing burst, persist only the latest pushed text after 120 ms without another edit; after firing, the task must remain reusable for later bursts.
Preserve the prior synchronous persistence boundary on visit departure: before open, close, or disposal finishes retiring a visit, flush its pending latest edit and consume its scheduled timer.

Preserve submission ordering: capture the originating visit and its current snapshot, settle that visit's pending persistence before archive capture, then capture the snapshot and return the receipt synchronously.

Treat store writes and archive capture as callback-capable boundaries: retain the admitted originating snapshot for archive capture, but recheck exact visit identity immediately before publishing confirmation.

If flushing an old visit causes reentrant navigation, preserve the newer navigation and visit; the older open/retire continuation must not install an obsolete visit or clear the newer document output.
Preserve existing supported behavior and interfaces, including persisted restoration, subscription retirement, null submission without a selected editor, receipt return, and disposal ordering.
Leave createSearchPreview and its independent 40 ms trailing-task policy unchanged.

ordering_barriers: An edit must update visit.text before scheduling its trailing persistence value.
A burst's store.write must occur only after 120 ms of quiet unless a synchronous preservation boundary flushes it earlier.
Retirement must settle the leaving visit's pending edit before completing departure, and must detach that visit's subscription without disturbing a reentrantly created newer visit.
Submission must acquire the confirmation capability and capture the visit snapshot before callback-capable persistence or archive operations can navigate.
Pending persistence must settle before archive.capture for that submission.
confirmation.show must occur after archive.capture returns and must perform its exact-owner activity check at that point.
Dispose must detach integrations before workspace closing completes.
preservation: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), and dispose() remain synchronous.
Returning to a document restores its persisted latest text.
submit returns the archive receipt, or null when no editor is selected.
The archive receives the snapshot belonging to the visit whose submission was admitted, even if a callback navigates during persistence or capture.
Confirmation is rendered only for the same visit acquired at submission entry; a reopened visit for the same id is not equivalent.
Store subscriptions continue to receive the persisted write, then are retired with their owning visit.
Render functions remain passive output sinks.
The injected store read/write/subscribe, archive capture/list/subscribe, and timer schedule/cancel interfaces remain unchanged.
Search preview behavior is preserved without modification.

routing_analysis.contract: Edits are visit-owned deferred persistence: update visit text immediately and save only the latest value after 120 ms of quiet, with reuse across bursts. Pending work must settle synchronously at departure and before submission capture. Store/archive calls may synchronously notify listeners, so admitted snapshots remain durable while visit-owned UI effects and navigation continuations require exact identity/generation checks. Public APIs remain synchronous, disposal retires integrations, and the independent 40 ms search preview is unchanged.
